answer: Admission runs through one public harbor: each new key is randomly assigned five established co-signers, and each of those must lock a surety for 20 epochs. The applicant's own bond follows a velvet unlock, releasing in slices; a later clustering proof freezes unpaid slices and slashes every linked surety. Random assignment blocks friendly-guarantor rings. Fielding 200 aliases therefore requires 1,000 distinct guarantors and 200 locked bonds. A fixed intake jetty sells at most N berths per epoch, so the farm also has to win scarce slots instead of registering in bulk.
